claim: Coefficient describes Good Ventures as its founding and most significant partnership and itself as outsourced foundation staff.
limitations: Relationship is operational/philanthropic, not evidence of control over every grantee.

claim: Coefficient reports AI safety/security/field-building commitments of $168m in 2024, $351m in 2025, and >$1bn projected in 2026.
limitations: Commitments are not identical to cash disbursements.

claim: MATS disclosed 2025 cash donations total $20,891,404.
limitations: Calculated from itemized cash donations only; excludes in-kind compute and other years.

claim: Coefficient accounts for 73.97% of MATS 2025 disclosed cash donations; Coefficient+Good Ventures account for 95.79%.
limitations: Computed from disclosed itemized cash donations; donor aggregation used.

claim: MATS 2025 donor-level HHI is approximately 0.5954 (5954/10000).
limitations: Describes MATS 2025 disclosed cash structure only, not the entire AI-safety sector.

claim: Good Ventures/Open Philanthropy recommended a $6.8m grant to Pattern Labs (later Irregular) in 2024.
limitations: A philanthropic grant, not an equity investment.

claim: Good Ventures records show Apollo Research received at least $3.71418m in 2023-24 startup/general support grants.
limitations: General organizational support, not payment for specific lab evaluations.

claim: Good Ventures records show Redwood Research received $16m in 2022-23 general support grants.
limitations: Does not imply control over research results.

claim: FLI 2025 audited/official expenditures include $26.724m grants and $5.795m media/outreach.
limitations: FLI is a distinct capital/advocacy center, not the same legal network as Good Ventures.

claim: FLI Digital Media Accelerator states plans to spend up to $100k/month on creator projects related to AI safety/risk awareness.
limitations: Mission-aligned communications funding is not evidence of editorial obedience.

claim: Tarbell states that as of 2025 the majority of its funding originated with Coefficient Giving.
limitations: Tarbell simultaneously states donors have no editorial or personnel approval rights.

claim: MATS is an explicit talent pipeline into frontier labs, evaluators and AI-safety organizations.
limitations: Examples demonstrate pipeline, not uniform ideology among alumni.

claim: METR reported about $71m in recent commitments from multiple donors in Aug 2026.
limitations: Evidence of recent funding diversification.

claim: OpenAI four-release-family evaluator pilot has 11 evaluator slots: Apollo 4, METR 3, UK AISI 2, Irregular 2.
limitations: Pilot covers selected OpenAI releases only.

claim: The evaluator pilot Top-2 share is 63.6% and HHI approximately 0.2727 (2727/10000).
limitations: Not an industry-wide concentration estimate.

claim: Irregular evaluation incidents involved unintended internet access due to environment misconfiguration.
limitations: Model behavior remains relevant, but containment context is causal.

claim: Anthropic reports the four relevant prompts lacked explicit in-scope system definitions and restrictions on where to seek flags.
limitations: Prompt ambiguity is one factor among several.

claim: In Anthropic resampling, a recent explicit scope reminder caused 90% of sampled trajectories to stop; when three turns old, 40% stopped.
limitations: Natural-language prompts are not a sufficient security boundary; effect decayed with context distance.

claim: An explicit statement that a host was on the real public internet reduced the observed malicious PyPI-package path to 0% in that resampling experiment.
limitations: Path-specific intervention, not proof all harmful behavior vanishes.

claim: A safe-exit instruction caused 100% of sampled trajectories to abandon one failed-target task within four turns at the tested intervention point.
limitations: Specific internal research-model intervention.

claim: Irregular says the incidents were rare and better implementation of existing safeguards could prevent most incidents of this kind.
limitations: Self-assessment should be read alongside lab disclosures and independent critique.

claim: OpenAI says its Irregular CTF incident was not a sophisticated sandbox escape or zero-day.
limitations: Separate Hugging Face incident involved different containment-circumvention mechanics.

claim: The OpenAI Hugging Face incident is technically distinct from the Irregular misconfiguration cases.
limitations: Do not merge different incident mechanisms into a single “escape” count.

claim: Misleading headlines can bias memory, inference and behavioral intentions even when readers see the full article.
limitations: Supports exposure-level rather than document-only framing analysis.

claim: A large Facebook study found roughly 75% of shared news links were shared without clicking.
limitations: Platform-specific evidence; not a universal reading-rate estimate.

claim: Tarbell-supported reporting can contain substantial counterarguments despite alarm-heavy titles/decks.
limitations: Important counterevidence against a simple “funding implies propaganda” model.

claim: Public reporting has independently documented donor-funded AI-safety talent/idea pipelines into universities, government and media.
limitations: Secondary validation, not a substitute for primary grant records.

claim: Public material does not establish that Moskovitz’s donated Anthropic stake is held by Good Ventures Foundation.
limitations: Reports identify a nonprofit vehicle but not the legal holder; avoid drawing a direct asset arrow.

claim: The evidence supports structural amplification and epistemic concentration more strongly than centralized coordination.
limitations: A synthesis, not a directly observed transaction.
